findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: The PR adds `int order();` as a new abstract method to the public SPI interface `CryptoProvider`. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (the interface is in keycloak-common and is loaded via ServiceLoader precisely so it can be implemented externally) will now fail to compile, and existing compiled implementations will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting. This should be a `default int order() { return 0; }` (or similar) method to remain backward compatible.

findings.title: Multiple providers with equal order are now silently accepted, can select non-FIPS provider in FIPS setup
findings.body: Previously, `detectProvider` threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath, which was a deliberate guard against misconfiguration. Now the code sorts by `order()` and silently picks the first. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return order 200, and `Stream.sorted` is stable, so ties are resolved by arbitrary ServiceLoader enumeration order. If both the default (non-FIPS) and the FIPS 140-2 crypto jars end up on the classpath (a realistic packaging mistake), Keycloak will now silently start with whichever provider the classloader happens to return first — potentially the non-FIPS one in a FIPS-required environment — instead of failing fast. The previously ignored providers are only logged at debug level, so this misconfiguration is easy to miss. At minimum, equal-order ties among distinct providers should still be an error (or the FIPS provider should have a strictly higher order and a warning logged at WARN level).

findings.title: Indefinite-length encoding (-1) is not handled, causing silent empty results or NegativeArraySizeException on malformed input
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for BER indefinite-length encoding (0x80). Callers do not handle this: `readSequence()` does `while (length > 0)` and silently returns an empty list for a -1 length (so `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` later fails with the misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2'), and `readNext()` computes `length += reset()` and calls `read(length)` with a negative value, throwing an unhelpful `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an IOException. Since this decoder parses signature bytes that ultimately come from a remote server, malformed/hostile input should produce a clear IOException. The -1 case should be rejected explicitly in `readLength()` (DER forbids indefinite lengths anyway) or handled by callers.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns whatever JCA provider services the default keystore type (e.g. the SUN provider), not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers of `CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` reasonably expect a BC/BCFIPS provider and may pass it into BC-specific APIs, which would fail or behave incorrectly in environments where this fallback provider is the one selected (i.e. standalone authz-client use). If no BouncyCastle provider is available, returning null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or throwing would be less misleading.
